symptom: MDL031 refused a view-entity CASE column declared String(8) — `case when … then l.Code when … then '0' + l.Code else '0000' end` over a String(8) Code — with "declared as String(8) but OQL expression returns String(200) … Fix: change to 'SortKey: String(200)'"; following the fix is CE6770 "View Entity is out of sync with the OQL Query", and exec ran the same check, so only --no-check wrote the declaration that builds. Numeric CASEs had the twin: `then 1 else 2.5` was typed Integer, refusing Decimal (the one that builds) and suggesting Integer (CE6770).
cause: inferCaseType returned the first branch it could TYPE. Without the project a bare attribute is untyped, so the later concatenation (derived, String(200)) decided. Mendix's rule is different per kind: a String CASE takes its FIRST branch's type, length included; a numeric CASE widens across ALL branches, Integer < Long < Decimal. The project-aware path never typed CASE branches at all (it fell back to the static inferrer), and typed a string literal at its own length instead of the derived 200.
file: mdl/executor/oql_type_inference.go (inferCaseType, caseResultExprs, numericRank; inferTypeFromExpression's CASE and literal branches; passthroughLengthError wording)
insight: Don't reason about the derivation rule — grid it. One mx check run over N expressions × every candidate declaration (lengths 1–16, 100, 108, 112, 200, unlimited; Integer/Long/Decimal) leaves exactly one accepted declaration per view, so the derived type reads straight off the survivors: 294 views, 20 s. The grid overturned the prior finding's 'a string-returning CASE is String(200)', which had only ever been measured on literal-first CASEs, and showed the two kinds follow DIFFERENT rules — `then l.Code else l.Name` (8, 100) is String(8), not the max, while `then l.IntV else l.LngV` is Long either way round. Had the fix been 'first branch decides' for every kind it would have kept the numeric false positive. The table of measurements is the test (oql_case_type_test.go): each row asserts the accepted declaration is never refused and, where check can judge, every other one is, with the accepted type as the Fix. A branch the checker cannot type must leave the result unknown wherever it could decide it — a first branch that is not a typed string, a numeric branch that could be wider — which is the issue's own 'or MDL031 is not raised when the length cannot be inferred'.
